record.original_question: Can motivic integration be generalized to Artin stacks in a way that is usable for McKay-correspondence-type results?

evidence.quote: Problem 10.3. Generalize the motivic integration to Artin stacks.

artifact.status_search_result: Significant progress has been made. Balwe developed p-adic and motivic measures on Artin n-stacks; Satriano–Usatine have developed motivic integration on (smooth) Artin stacks with a change-of-variables formula, and used it to prove a McKay correspondence for linearly reductive groups and to show that varieties with log-terminal singularities admit crepant resolutions by smooth Artin stacks (Duke Math. J. 2024). A fully general theory subsuming all McKay-correspondence settings (e.g., wild and non-reductive cases) does not yet appear complete, so the problem is best regarded as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Crepant resolutions of log-terminal singularities via Artin stacks
status_evidence.snippet: Every variety with log-terminal singularities admits a crepant resolution by a smooth Artin stack, and new McKay correspondences express stringy invariants of Q-Gorenstein varieties in terms of motivic integrals on arc spaces of smooth stacks.
status_evidence.claim: Motivic integration on smooth Artin stacks has been developed sufficiently to give McKay-type correspondences and crepant stacky resolutions.

status_evidence.title: p-adic and Motivic Measure on Artin n-stacks
status_evidence.snippet: Construction of p-adic and motivic measures on Artin n-stacks.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier work generalized motivic and p-adic measures to Artin n-stacks.

status_evidence.title: Beyond twisted arcs: a McKay correspondence for reductive groups
status_evidence.snippet: A motivic change of variables formula expressing motivic integrals over arcs of singular varieties as motivic integrals over warped arcs of Artin stack resolutions, yielding a McKay correspondence for linearly reductive groups.
status_evidence.claim: A change-of-variables formula on Artin stacks yields a McKay correspondence for linearly reductive groups.
